12-25.name: St. Bessarion the Great
12-25.summary: A 4th-century Egyptian ascetic who trained under Anba Anthony and Anba Macarius before withdrawing into the desert, owning nothing but a coarse garment and the Gospels. Known for walking on water, sweetening salt water for a thirsty companion, healing a paralyzed child, and guiding St. Taor to repentance.

12-25.name: Pope Macarius III, 114th Patriarch of Alexandria
12-25.summary: Born in El-Mahalla El-Koubra, became a monk at St. Pishoy Monastery, served as Bishop of Assiut for 47 years, then Pope of Alexandria from 1944 until his death in 1945. His short papacy included reforms on divorce law, family legislation, and monastic education.

12-27.name: Sts. Benjamin and his sister Eudoxia
12-27.summary: Two siblings born in Shabsheer, Egypt, to pious Christian parents devoted to hospitality and asceticism. Benjamin, longing to shed his blood for Christ, confessed his faith before the governor of Shatanof and was tortured and imprisoned; his sister Eudoxia refused to be separated from him, choosing to die with him rather than leave his side. Both were martyred together after the governor bound them with heavy stones and threw them into the river, from which they were miraculously freed by an angel before ultimately winning their crowns of martyrdom.
